image.subject: Edmond Dantès, a lean dark-haired young sailor in his late teens to twenties, sunburnt face gone gaunt, lies motionless on a chained iron bed in a damp stone prison cell on the Château d'If, turned toward the wall, 1815

storyboard.claim: Dantès is starving himself to death in silence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gaunt Dantès curled on a chained iron bed, face to the wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the cell scene after the chapter setup.
storyboard.addedInformation: His physical collapse, sea and boots only heard.

image.subject: an elderly white-haired Italian priest, thin and stooped, ragged black cassock, long untrimmed white beard, climbing out of a ragged hole broken through a damp stone prison wall, 1815

storyboard.claim: An old priest emerges from behind the wall.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Faria's head and shoulders coming through a crumbling hole in the stone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows Dantès's collapse in the bed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Faria's look and the wall breach.

image.subject: a small clay lamp burning animal fat, its weak flame flickering on a stone ledge in a freezing damp prison cell, rough walls, 1815

storyboard.claim: Light comes from a crude lamp of rendered animal fat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flickering lamp on a stone ledge in the cell.

image.subject: an elderly white-haired priest in a ragged black cassock, holding up a half-burnt scrap of parchment map in the flickering light of a lamp in a stone prison cell, 1815

storyboard.claim: Faria holds a half-burnt treasure map.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Faria holding a scorched parchment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues from the lamp in the cell.
storyboard.addedInformation: The map is burnt at one edge.

image.subject: a close view of a half-burnt yellowed parchment, its faded reddish-brown ink in heavy gothic handwriting too worn to read, lit by a flickering lamp, 1815

storyboard.claim: The map's ink is reddish and its letters gothic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Close view of faded reddish gothic script on parchment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Zooms into the map held by Faria.

image.subject: a hand-drawn chart of a rocky uninhabited Mediterranean island, with a small inked cross marking a spot on its coast, on old parchment, 1815

storyboard.claim: The map leads to the uninhabited island of Monte Cristo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Rocky island outline with an inked cross.
storyboard.addedInformation: The island is uninhabited and the mark shows the spot.

storyboard.claim: Knowledge is the ultimate untraceable capital.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.

image.subject: Edmond Dantès and the elderly Abbé Faria sitting face to face on the floor of a pitch-black stone cell, a single candle stub between them, 1815

storyboard.claim: Power is made in the dark between the two men.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two men facing each other across one candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narration shifts to the mechanism of power.
storyboard.addedInformation: Both prisoners in the same cell.

storyboard.claim: Dantès gets intellectual wealth before any gold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.

storyboard.claim: The education is a transfer that defies belief.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrator introduces the mechanics of the teaching.
storyboard.addedInformation: No new facts, a framing beat.

image.subject: an elderly priest in a ragged black cassock leaning over a young sailor in a stone prison cell, pointing at letters scratched into the wall, 1815

storyboard.claim: Faria teaches Dantès five living languages.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Faria pointing at scratched letters for Dantès.
storyboard.addedInformation: The teaching happens by pointing at a wall.

storyboard.claim: Faria also teaches maths, physics and aristocratic politics.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Four-line list of subjects.

image.subject: an empty stone prison cell with bare damp walls, a tin plate on the floor and nothing else, a grey light from a high barred window, 1815

storyboard.claim: The cell has no books, no paper and no pens.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bare cell with only a tin plate.

image.subject: an elderly priest in a ragged black cassock mixing soot and wine in a tin cup on a stone ledge, a sharpened fish bone beside it, in a damp prison cell, 1815

storyboard.claim: Faria makes ink from soot and wine and pens from fish bone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tin cup of soot and wine, fish bone beside it.

image.subject: a torn strip of white linen cloth from a shirt, covered edge to edge in dense brown handwriting in ink, laid on a rough stone floor, 1815

storyboard.claim: Faria writes on scraps of linen torn from his own shirts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Linen scrap covered in brown writing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the ink and pen beat.

image.subject: an elderly white-haired priest in a ragged black cassock resting a gentle hand on the shoulder of a young sailor in a stone prison cell, a lamp glowing between them, 1815

storyboard.claim: Faria is the savior figure the narrator has always seen.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Faria's hand on a young man's shoulder.

image.subject: Edmond Dantès, a lean dark-haired young sailor, sitting upright on a chained iron bed in a stone prison cell, colour slowly returning to his sunburnt face, a clay bowl of food beside him, 1815

storyboard.claim: Faria breathes life back into the starving man.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dantès sitting up, a little colour in his face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrast with the collapsed Dantès at the start.

storyboard.claim: Faria resurrects Edmond Dantès with a father figure, education and a fortune.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fortune is named as a result.

storyboard.claim: Faria did not save Dantès.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Punchline text on the screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the rescue on its head.

storyboard.claim: Faria, the narrator thinks, cursed him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.

storyboard.claim: Giving someone the intellectual keys to the universe is a curse without an emotional foundation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrator asks how that could be a curse.

image.subject: Edmond Dantès, a lean dark-haired young sailor, sitting in a stone prison cell with a hard, hollow stare, his face set in grief and anger, 1815

storyboard.claim: Faria gave Dantès the intellectual weapons of a god but left him emotionally devastated.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dantès hard-faced, grief set into him.

image.subject: Edmond Dantès and the elderly Abbé Faria bent over a table in a stone prison cell, scraps of linen with names written on them spread between them in candlelight, 1815

storyboard.claim: Faria helps Dantès logically deduce who betrayed him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two men over linen scraps of names.
storyboard.addedInformation: The deduction happens on the linen.

storyboard.claim: Faria walks Dantès through the timeline, the motives and the players.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.

left.label: DANGLARS
left.subject: a stout middle-aged clerk in a dark suit and high white collar, neat side-parted hair, sallow cautious face, 1815 Marseille ship's accountant turned Paris banker

right.label: FERNAND
right.subject: a handsome dark-haired young Catalan fisherman in a faded blue jacket, a jealous sullen look, 1815 Marseille

storyboard.claim: Dantès realises what Danglars and Fernand did.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Side-by-side portraits of Danglars and Fernand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrator names the two men in the deduction.

image.subject: Edmond Dantès in a stone prison cell, his face half in dark shadow, a cold terrible expression, while an elderly priest draws back from him in alarm, 1815

storyboard.claim: A dark shadow crosses Dantès's face and Faria recoils.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dantès half in shadow, Faria stepping back.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the deduction of the two men.

image.subject: a loaded flintlock pistol lying on a rough wooden table beside a folded letter, in the dim light of a candle, 1815

storyboard.claim: Faria regrets handing a loaded weapon to a man consumed by revenge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Pistol on a table beside a letter.
storyboard.addedInformation: The weapon image stands for the revenge.

storyboard.claim: Faria planted the seed of divine retribution.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.

storyboard.claim: Faria armed a devastated man to become a monster.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.

image.subject: a heap of gold coins spilling across a dark wooden table beside a guttering candle, 1830s, untouched by any hand

storyboard.claim: Infinite knowledge and infinite wealth on a bleeding soul do not make a philanthropist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Heap of gold coins by a candle.

image.subject: a barred window casting thin bars of grey light across the stone floor of an empty damp prison cell, 1815

storyboard.claim: The intellectual capital is the foundation of the psychological prison Dantès builds for his enemies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barred window light across a cell floor.
storyboard.addedInformation: The prison is mental, the bars are light.

image.subject: a pitch-black stone prison cell, the only light a single candle that has just gone out, a thin wisp of smoke rising, 1815

storyboard.claim: Latency is the mechanism of the prison, knowledge compounding in the dark.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Pitch black cell after a candle goes out.

image.subject: an old brass hourglass standing on a damp stone ledge, sand running through its neck in a dim prison cell, 1815

storyboard.claim: Faria teaches that time is a physical weight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hourglass on a stone ledge.

storyboard.claim: The prisoners turn patience into a weapon, against the men who jailed Dantès.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.

storyboard.claim: The betrayal is a study in the banality of evil.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from the cell to the betrayal.

image.subject: the shaded leafy arbour of a waterside inn outside Marseille, white tablecloths under vines, a few wooden chairs, 1815

storyboard.claim: The scene moves to the arbour of the inn at Le Réserve outside Marseille.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Leafy arbour with tables under vines.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cut from the cell to the sunlit inn.
storyboard.addedInformation: The place of the betrothal feast.

image.subject: the glittering blue Mediterranean seen through the branches of an olive tree on a bright sunny day, 1815

storyboard.claim: It is a bright sunny day, birds singing, the sea glittering behind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Glittering sea through olive branches.
storyboard.addedInformation: Bright light versus the cell's dark.

image.subject: a stout middle-aged clerk in a dark suit and high white collar sitting alone at a corner table, away from the dancing guests in a sunlit arbour, 1815 Marseille

storyboard.claim: At Dantès's betrothal feast, Danglars sits alone in a corner, away from the dancing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Danglars alone at a corner table, guests dancing behind.
storyboard.addedInformation: Danglars is isolated at the feast.

image.subject: an open ship's ledger on a table with columns of handwritten figures and a pen laid across the page, 1815 Marseille

storyboard.claim: Danglars is a man defined by numbers and bureaucracy, the ship's supercargo who keeps the ledgers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Open ledger with columns of figures.

storyboard.claim: Danglars hates Dantès because Dantès is a variable he cannot control.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.
storyboard.addedInformation: The motive is control, not hate.
